cells.B: Leadership is central to greatness; those in power must hold themselves to the highest standard.
Aligns with modern leadership theories emphasizing self-accountability and leading by example.
Leaders model behavior and inspire others through personal integrity and high moral standards (Bass & Riggio, 2006).
Focus on humility, self-awareness, and service over authority (Greenleaf, 1977; Spears, 2010).
Leaders demonstrate moral courage and responsibility, acting as ethical role models (Brown & Treviño, 2006).
Emphasizes authenticity, self-knowledge, and front-line leadership (Bennis, 2009).
Leadership as evolving, self-critical, and courageous in the face of change (Heifetz & Linsky, 2002).
Power is a responsibility; leaders must catalyze performance through self-discipline (Kouzes & Posner, 2017).
Leadership is defined not by authority alone, but by self-imposed discipline and example setting.
